details:
Field Shift is a web-based agricultural decision-support system that transforms NASA POWER climate data into practical and explainable crop-planning insights. The project was developed as a Bursa pilot, but its data pipeline is designed to work with geographic coordinates and can be extended to other regions.

The user selects a location and enters the previous crop, planned crop, next-period crop, soil type, production priority, and planned harvest dates. Field Shift automatically determines the latest five completed calendar years. For example, an analysis performed in 2026 uses data from 2021–2025. The backend retrieves daily temperature, precipitation, humidity, and root-zone wetness data from NASA POWER. It uses caching, controlled retries, concurrent-request deduplication, and a verified fallback dataset to remain functional during temporary service limitations. The interface also shows whether the result came from live NASA data, cache, or the verified fallback source.

Our climate-analysis module calculates average, minimum, and maximum temperatures, total precipitation, dry days, hot days, the longest dry period, monthly climate patterns, data completeness, and an explainable climate-risk score. The system preserves genuine zero values and continues operating when optional humidity or soil-wetness fields are unavailable. It also compares the user’s planned harvest window with the same calendar period across five historical seasons. This provides average temperature, maximum temperature, precipitation, rainy-day frequency, extreme-heat frequency, and data completeness for the selected harvest period.

The recommendation engine evaluates the planned crop using climate suitability, water demand, soil compatibility, crop rotation rules, and the farmer’s selected priority. It then provides up to three ranked alternatives with individual climate, water, soil, and rotation scores. Each recommendation includes benefits and cautions so that users can understand why the system produced the result.

Field Shift differs from a standard weather dashboard because it connects historical climate evidence, harvest timing, crop suitability, and crop rotation in one workflow. It does not claim to predict future weather. Instead, it supports forward-looking agricultural decisions using the latest five completed years of historical evidence.

The project uses Python 3.14, FastAPI, JSON-based module contracts, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet, and NASA POWER services. It runs in a standard web browser and requires no specialized hardware. Public data, open-source components, and caching make the prototype suitable for a low-cost pilot.

We validated the system with 178 automated tests. In the Bursa end-to-end scenario, the API returned HTTP 200, analyzed five historical seasons, generated the harvest-period climate summary, evaluated the planned crop, and returned up to three ranked alternatives. Current limitations include the Bursa-focused pilot dataset and the use of historical evidence rather than a weather forecast. Field Shift supports farmers and agricultural experts; it does not replace local agronomic expertise.
Super Intelligence tools assisted with brainstorming, research, code development, debugging, writing, translation, visual design, and presentation preparation. The team reviewed, tested, and integrated all final outputs.
